chapters.note: The changes of ritual agent are retained, including the plural priests in 1:9 and the singular priest in 1:13. The change from “you” to “he” in 1:14 is also retained. “Acceptable” and the repeated “sweet savour” remain.
The grain-offering instructions retain their repeated references to oil, frankincense, salt and the memorial portion. The prohibition in 2:11 has clearer English word order; its scope is retained.
The repeated descriptions of fat and the perpetual prohibition on eating fat and blood remain. Conditional clauses now use ordinary present-tense English.

The distinct offerings for the anointed priest, congregation, ruler and individual are retained. Reordered clauses make the agent of pouring the blood clearer without changing the sequence of actions.
The source numbering continues through 5:26. Clauses about knowledge, guilt, restitution and the added fifth are retained; modern verb forms clarify their English connections.
Source numbering begins this chapter with the altar instructions. Reordering clarifies who eats the remainder and where blood is washed; the ritual objects and repeated commands remain.
The distinctions among offerings, participants and permitted days of eating remain. “Morrow” is retained where it is clear; present-tense verb endings follow the current Bespoke convention.
The repeated instructions for consecration, vestments and offerings remain. In 8:35, “so that you do not die” clarifies the negative purpose clause.
The sequence of offerings, blessing, appearance of glory and fire remains. The shift between Moses, Aaron, the priests and the people is preserved.
The narrative and restrictions following the deaths of Nadab and Abihu retain their separate speakers. Address to Aaron and his household uses “you” and “your”.

The received animal names and classification language remain provisional. “Hands”, “cud” and the distinctions among touching, carrying and eating are retained; these names have not received a new specialist zoological review.

The periods of uncleanness and purification, their distinct durations and the alternative offering remain. The opening conditional and the instruction about sixty-six days have clearer English grammar.
The sequences of inspection, waiting and re-examination remain. The received descriptions of lesions, hair, colour and garments are retained without claiming a modern medical diagnosis.

The inherited negative in 14:39, “not spread”, is retained after a selected check of the Rahlfs–Hanhart main text. The ritual sequences and alternative offerings remain; no critical-apparatus decision is claimed.
The distinctions among bodily conditions, contact, washing and waiting remain. In 15:31, the negative purpose clause now reads “so that they do not die”.

The distinct instructions for the two goats, the sanctuary, altar and people remain. The inherited “sent away” wording is retained; this edition does not resolve the wider interpretive question through an added gloss.
The repeated language of blood, life and atonement remains. Modern verb forms do not change the stated subjects or the distinction between slaughtering and hunting.

Ordinary address uses “you” and “your”. The opening contrast with the practices of Egypt and Canaan has clearer English word order; the repeated prohibitions and the image of the land’s response remain.

The repeated divine self-identification remains. Commands concerning neighbour, resident stranger, justice and measures retain their distinct objects. The inherited “upon the mountains” in 19:26 is retained after a selected main-text check.
The prohibitions, stated consequences and recurring language of sanctification remain. Modern verb endings clarify the English while preserving the inherited distinctions.
The distinctions among priests, the high priest and the listed bodily conditions remain. Received physical descriptions are retained without a new specialist identification claim.
Reordering in 22:23–24 and 22:28 clarifies the relation between the animal and the instruction. The distinction between offerings and the prohibition concerning mother and young remains.
The sequence of observances and repeated prohibitions on work remain. “Morrow” and “first day” in 23:11 are retained; the sentence now places the priest before the action.
The instructions about lamps and bread, the intervening narrative and the legal declarations remain. The different objects of striking in the closing laws are preserved.

Release, redemption, land and labour remain distinct. The inherited “sixth year of release” in 25:28 is retained after a selected Rahlfs–Hanhart main-text check. It is not silently replaced by a more familiar reading.
The repeated conditional structure, consequences and covenant language remain. “You” and “your” serve ordinary address; divine first-person capitals are retained as an editorial convention.
The distinct rules for valuations, redemption, devoted things and tithes remain. The added fifth and the stated exceptions are retained; 27:8 has clearer subject–verb order.

scope: English editorial review; selected main-text checks; all earlier notes retained as history. No new full independent source, apparatus, reception or human read-aloud review.
